### Development and writing
It also ranked number 18 on _Collider_'s list of "The 20 Best Drama Movies of the 2020s So Far," calling it "one of the definitive crowd pleasers of the decade."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-drama-4)_MovieWeb_ ranked it number 15 on its list of the "20 Most Underrated Films of the Last 5 Years," writing that "it certainly deserves way more credit" and called it "groundbreaking in its representation of disability."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-64)
In 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of _The New York Times_' list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century," finishing at number 280.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-65)
At the 94th Academy Awards, _CODA_ won all three awards that it was nominated for: Best Picture, Best Supporting Actor (Kotsur), and Best Adapted Screenplay.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-Oscars-66) It is the first film produced or distributed by a streaming service, the first Sundance film, and the first film featuring predominantly deaf actors in leading roles to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-67) The film had the fewest nominations for a Best Picture winner since 1932's _Grand Hotel_, and is also the sixth film and the first since 2018's _Green Book_ to win Best Picture without a director nomination.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-68)

### Development and writing
_CODA_ was nominated for Best Motion Picture - Drama and Best Supporting Actor (for Kotsur) at the 79th Golden Globe Awards. It received three nominations at the 75th British Academy Film Awards, winning two, including Best Supporting Actor for Kotsur, making him the first deaf person to ever win a BAFTA, and Best Adapted Screenplay for Heder. At the 28th Screen Actors Guild Awards, the film made history with Kotsur, Matlin and Durant becoming the first deaf/non-hearing performers to win, along with Jones, Derbez and Walsh-Peelo, for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-69) At the 33rd Producers Guild of America Awards, the film was also awarded the Producers Guild of America Award for Best Theatrical Motion Picture.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-PGA-70)
_CODA_ was one of 28 films that received the ReFrame Stamp for 2021, awarded by the gender equity coalition ReFrame for films that are proven to have gender-balanced hiring.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-ReFrame-71) The film was also given the Seal of Authentic Representation from the Ruderman Family Foundation for Matlin's and Durant's roles as Ruby's mother and brother. The seal is given to films and series that feature actors with disabilities who have at least five lines of dialogue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-72)

## Planned stage musical adaptation
[edit]
On March 23, 2022, it was reported by _The New York Times_ that, in an effort to keep the film relevant after awards season, its producers plan to team up with Deaf West Theatre to develop a stage musical adaptation of the film, with a creative team and production scheduled yet to be announced. DJ Kurs, Deaf West's artistic director, expressed excitement for the project: "As a Deaf person, I knew from the start that _CODA_ would make a perfect musical: It addresses our relationship with music and how we move through the world of sound like immigrants in a foreign country, learning new, seemingly arbitrary rules on the fly." Like Deaf West's production of _Spring Awakening_, the musical will incorporate both signing in American Sign Language and live singing.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-musical-73)
The report also noted that Rousselet had been asked in 2014 about making a stage version of _La Famille Bélier_, but that he and the producers wanted to prioritize making _CODA_ and forging a relationship with Deaf West first. Rousselet further remarked "It's going to be a new adventure for us. But I think it has everything – the characters, the music, the wonderful environment – to make a beautiful musical." Kotsur said that he hopes the musical will have its initial staging within two years; he seemed to suggest that he might reprise his role as Frank in the production.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-musical-73) Kurs noted his desire to have Matlin and Durant also reprise their roles as Jackie and Leo, respectively, along with Kotsur.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-74)
In August 2024, Deaf West Theatre announced its 2024–25 season and officially confirmed that the musical is still in the works.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-75)

About Rifkin's Festival
Titular Mort Rifkin (**Wallace Shawn** - _My Dinner with Andre_) is an ill-at-ease retired film professor who accompanies his wife, Sue (**Gina Gershon** - _Bound_), to the San Sebastian Film Festival, mainly because he's jealous of her friendship with up-and-coming director Philippe (**Louis Garrel** - _A Faithful Man_). The neurotic negotiations over fading relationships, love triangles, artistic sensibility, and the passage of time are all on display, swirling around the picturesque Spanish setting.
**_Travel in style..._**

### Development and writing
It also ranked number 18 on _Collider_'s list of "The 20 Best Drama Movies of the 2020s So Far," calling it "one of the definitive crowd pleasers of the decade."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-drama-4)_MovieWeb_ ranked it number 15 on its list of the "20 Most Underrated Films of the Last 5 Years," writing that "it certainly deserves way more credit" and called it "groundbreaking in its representation of disability."[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-64)
In 2025, it was one of the films voted for the "Readers' Choice" edition of _The New York Times_' list of "The 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century," finishing at number 280.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-65)
At the 94th Academy Awards, _CODA_ won all three awards that it was nominated for: Best Picture, Best Supporting Actor (Kotsur), and Best Adapted Screenplay.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-Oscars-66) It is the first film produced or distributed by a streaming service, the first Sundance film, and the first film featuring predominantly deaf actors in leading roles to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-67) The film had the fewest nominations for a Best Picture winner since 1932's _Grand Hotel_, and is also the sixth film and the first since 2018's _Green Book_ to win Best Picture without a director nomination.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-68)
texts.19:
### Development and writing
_CODA_ was nominated for Best Motion Picture - Drama and Best Supporting Actor (for Kotsur) at the 79th Golden Globe Awards. It received three nominations at the 75th British Academy Film Awards, winning two, including Best Supporting Actor for Kotsur, making him the first deaf person to ever win a BAFTA, and Best Adapted Screenplay for Heder. At the 28th Screen Actors Guild Awards, the film made history with Kotsur, Matlin and Durant becoming the first deaf/non-hearing performers to win, along with Jones, Derbez and Walsh-Peelo, for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-69) At the 33rd Producers Guild of America Awards, the film was also awarded the Producers Guild of America Award for Best Theatrical Motion Picture.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-PGA-70)
_CODA_ was one of 28 films that received the ReFrame Stamp for 2021, awarded by the gender equity coalition ReFrame for films that are proven to have gender-balanced hiring.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-ReFrame-71) The film was also given the Seal of Authentic Representation from the Ruderman Family Foundation for Matlin's and Durant's roles as Ruby's mother and brother. The seal is given to films and series that feature actors with disabilities who have at least five lines of dialogue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-72)
texts.20:
## Planned stage musical adaptation
[edit]
On March 23, 2022, it was reported by _The New York Times_ that, in an effort to keep the film relevant after awards season, its producers plan to team up with Deaf West Theatre to develop a stage musical adaptation of the film, with a creative team and production scheduled yet to be announced. DJ Kurs, Deaf West's artistic director, expressed excitement for the project: "As a Deaf person, I knew from the start that _CODA_ would make a perfect musical: It addresses our relationship with music and how we move through the world of sound like immigrants in a foreign country, learning new, seemingly arbitrary rules on the fly." Like Deaf West's production of _Spring Awakening_, the musical will incorporate both signing in American Sign Language and live singing.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-musical-73)
The report also noted that Rousselet had been asked in 2014 about making a stage version of _La Famille Bélier_, but that he and the producers wanted to prioritize making _CODA_ and forging a relationship with Deaf West first. Rousselet further remarked "It's going to be a new adventure for us. But I think it has everything – the characters, the music, the wonderful environment – to make a beautiful musical." Kotsur said that he hopes the musical will have its initial staging within two years; he seemed to suggest that he might reprise his role as Frank in the production.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-musical-73) Kurs noted his desire to have Matlin and Durant also reprise their roles as Jackie and Leo, respectively, along with Kotsur.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-74)
In August 2024, Deaf West Theatre announced its 2024–25 season and officially confirmed that the musical is still in the works.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CODA_(2021_film)#cite_note-75)
